name: Macfarlane Group PLC
executive_summary: Macfarlane Group PLC is a UK protective packaging distributor and manufacturer that the quantitative screen rates **buy** (4/22 models; composite score 57%), supported by cheapness (P/B 0.9, FCF yield ~15.6%), dividend, GARP, and risk factor passes across all four families. The stock trades below book with a ~5.3% yield and sustained free cash flow despite a sharp FY2025 earnings collapse—net income fell ~59% to £6.3m on revenue up ~11% to £300.8m (Yahoo fallback). The central debate is whether the profit downturn—driven by UK distribution pricing pressure, cost inflation, and disruption from a fatal accident at a recently acquired site—is cyclical or marks a structural step-down in returns. Primary filing body extracts are unavailable in this pack; financial analysis relies on Yahoo fallback and news flow, limiting verification of going-concern language, covenant detail, and interim trends.
investment_thesis:
For a value investor, MACF.L presents a “cash-rich, earnings-poor” profile. The screen passes FCF Yield, Neff PEGY (0.04), Dividend Growth, and Earnings Quality, with full data quality (20/20 metrics) and building conviction (39%, three weeks at signal, stable). At P/E 16.8 on depressed FY2025 earnings but P/B 0.9 and ROE 5.2%, the market appears to capitalise trough profits while anchoring on balance-sheet value and cash generation.

Business quality is mixed but not broken. Revenue grew to £300.8m in FY2025 (Yahoo fallback), consistent with management commentary on continued top-line expansion via bolt-on M&A and market share gains in UK packaging distribution and manufacturing. Operating cash flow remained robust at £24.8m and free cash flow at £20.1m (Yahoo), supporting dividends (~£5.8m paid) and ongoing share buybacks (65.55–68p per share, July 2026). Net debt rose to £16.2m but remains modest relative to EBITDA (~£31.1m, ~0.5x net debt/EBITDA).

The buy case rests on mean reversion: if operating margins recover from FY2025’s compressed £12.5m operating profit (from £23.6m in FY2024), earnings power could re-rate the stock without multiple expansion. Institutional ownership (~83%) and active capital return reinforce a shareholder-friendly overlay. Screen-reported earnings growth of −68.2% reflects the trough; the Neff PEGY pass suggests the market may already discount much of the downturn.
financial_review:
**Source limitation:** The filings index catalogues five annual Companies House accounts (filed May 2022 through May 2026; regime `uk_rns`, source `companies_house`) but **none have downloadable body extracts** (`with_body: 0`; refetch attempted on all five, zero fetched). **No interim or half-year RNS filings** are indexed. All figures below are from `financials_annual.json` (Yahoo fallback); treat as indicative pending verified annual report review.

**Income statement trend (Yahoo, £000s unless stated):**

| Metric | FY2022 | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY2025 |
|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|
| Revenue | 290,431 | 280,714 | 270,437 | 300,810 |
| Operating income | 21,496 | 22,068 | 23,597 | 12,495 |
| EBITDA | 34,289 | 36,186 | 39,402 | 31,087 |
| Pretax profit | 19,934 | 20,280 | 20,896 | 8,050 |
| Net income | 15,637 | 14,974 | 15,530 | 6,316 |
| Diluted EPS (p) | 9.78 | 9.34 | 9.74 | 3.98 |

FY2025 marks a clear inflection: revenue rose ~11% to £300.8m (consistent with *“Macfarlane’s 2025 profitability tumbles amid tough market”*, Yahoo Finance, 2 Mar 2026) but net income fell ~59% to £6.3m and diluted EPS fell to 3.98p. Operating margin compressed from ~8.7% (FY2024) to ~4.2% (FY2025). Interest expense increased to £5.0m (from £3.1m), further pressuring pretax profit.

FY2022–FY2024 showed relatively stable earnings (~£15–16m net income) on flattish-to-declining revenue, suggesting FY2025’s margin collapse—not top-line weakness—is the primary concern.

**Cash flow (Yahoo):** Operating cash flow held at £24.8m (FY2025) vs £25.4m (FY2024). Free cash flow was £20.1m (FY2025), £22.5m (FY2024), and peaked at £31.3m (FY2023). FY2025 included £12.9m acquisition spend and £4.6m capex. FCF materially exceeded net income in FY2025, supporting the screen’s FCF Yield pass—but the gap may reflect working-capital movements and non-cash charges rather than sustainable economic earnings.

**Balance sheet (Yahoo, FY2025):** Total assets £277.8m; equity £120.6m; total debt £89.4m (including capital lease obligations £58.8m); net debt £16.2m (up from £1.9m in FY2024). Goodwill and intangibles total £104.9m versus tangible book value of only £15.6m—significant acquisition goodwill creates impairment sensitivity if margins stay depressed. Defined benefit pension liability: £6.0m on balance sheet (down from £9.6m in FY2024). Working capital turned negative (−£1.5m vs +£13.1m prior year).

**Dividends and capital return:** Cash dividends paid £5.8m in both FY2025 and FY2024—held flat despite earnings halving, implying a higher payout ratio and sustainability question. Share buybacks: £2.1m (FY2025).

**Interim gap:** No half-year results, trading updates, or RNS body text are available in the index. H2 FY2025 commentary (*“Macfarlane Group H2 Earnings Call Highlights”*, Yahoo Finance, 3 Mar 2026) describes the year as “tough” with intense UK pricing competition and accident-related disruption, but interim financial detail cannot be cross-checked against primary filings.
risks_and_flags:
**Earnings and cyclicality:** FY2025 profitability “tumbled” amid UK packaging distribution price competition and higher operating costs (*“Resilient revenue for Macfarlane Group despite 59% dip in annual profit”*, Scottish Financial News, 26 Feb 2026). Without filing bodies, margin bridge, segment detail, and forward guidance cannot be verified.

**Operational and regulatory:** Management cited operational and financial disruption from a **fatal accident at a recently acquired business** at Pitreavie (*“Macfarlane warns on profits following Pitreavie fatality”*, Printweek, 22 Oct 2025; H2 earnings call highlights, 3 Mar 2026). Potential HSE investigation, remediation costs, reputational damage, and insurance/contingency exposures are unquantified in available sources.

**Balance sheet and goodwill:** Goodwill (£74.5m) plus intangibles (£30.4m) exceed tangible equity; sustained margin weakness raises impairment risk not captured by static screen metrics.

**Leverage and leases:** Total debt rose to £89.4m; capitalised leases £58.8m. Interest expense nearly doubled year-on-year. Net debt/EBITDA remains manageable (~0.5x) but the direction is unfavourable.

**Pension:** Balance-sheet defined benefit obligation £6.0m persists (Yahoo). News reports a £53m pension scheme buy-in (*“Macfarlane Group secures £53m pension scheme buy-in”*, Investing.com, 30 Jun 2026), which would materially de-risk long-term funding but cannot be reconciled to statutory disclosures without annual report body text. Full triennial valuation, buy-in accounting treatment, and any remaining deficit are unverified.

**Dividend sustainability:** Flat dividend against halved earnings; third-party commentary explicitly warns dividend investors (*“Dividend Investors: Don't Be Too Quick To Buy Macfarlane Group PLC (LON:MACF) For Its Upcoming Dividend”*, Simply Wall St, 11 May 2026). Payout is supported by FCF today but vulnerable if cash conversion weakens.

**Governance / disclosure gap:** Five Companies House annual accounts are indexed but bodies were not extracted—going-concern statements, covenant terms, contingent liabilities, and related-party disclosures cannot be reviewed. This is a material research gap.

**Market sentiment:** One-year share price loss linked to shrinking earnings (*“The one-year loss for Macfarlane Group (LON:MACF) shareholders likely driven by its shrinking earnings”*, Yahoo Finance, 28 Nov 2025); screen timing signal is “insufficient_data.”

**Context / analytical:**

- *“Declining Stock and Decent Financials: Is The Market Wrong About Macfarlane Group PLC (LON:MACF)?”* (Yahoo Finance, 22 Jan 2026): Explores valuation disconnect.

**Thin areas:** No indexed news on major M&A beyond bolt-on commentary, management changes, or regulatory enforcement actions in the past year beyond accident-related reporting. Broader FTSE/mid-cap and dividend-listicle pieces dominate the feed.
research_rationale: Quantitative cheapness and FCF metrics are partially confirmed by sustained cash generation and sub-book valuation, but the FY2025 earnings collapse, goodwill-heavy balance sheet, and absence of primary filing bodies prevent full confirmation of the screen’s buy signal.
